Unimodal and Sigmoid Shapes

Source: R/shape.R
shape_located.Rd

Construct the shapes of scs() that have a location: shape_unimodal() rises to a mode and falls after it (or, with valley = TRUE, falls to a minimum and rises after it); shape_sigmoid() increases (or, with decreasing = TRUE, decreases) with a slope that grows up to an inflection and shrinks after it.

Usage

shape_unimodal(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  mode = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  valley = FALSE,
  value = NULL,
  mode_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_sigmoid(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  inflection = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  decreasing = FALSE,
  value = NULL,
  inflection_by = c("level", "shared")
)

Arguments

link

A linkfunctions7 link onto \((0, \infty)\).

mode, inflection

NULL, a single number (the value of the covariate at which the mode or the inflection is placed), or a vector of such numbers named by the levels of a factor by.

index

NULL, the index \(M\) itself, or a vector of indices named by level. A fitting layer sets it on the versions it tries. It takes precedence over mode and inflection.

valley

FALSE for a maximum, TRUE for a minimum, or a logical vector named by level.

value

NULL, two finite numbers c(at = a, value = v), or a list list(at = a, value = v) whose elements are one number or a vector named by level: the smooth is \(v\) at \(a\), in place of the centering (see shape_increasing() for when \(v\) changes the fit).

mode_by, inflection_by

Under a factor by, whether a location that is not given is chosen for each level ("level", the default) or once for every level ("shared"). "shared" without a factor by is an error.

decreasing

FALSE for an increasing sigmoid, TRUE for a decreasing one, or a logical vector named by level.

Value

An S7 object of class ShapeUnimodal or ShapeSigmoid, both inheriting from ShapeLocated and shape_constraint.

Where the location sits

The location is an index \(M\) of the Greville abscissae \(\xi_1 < \dots < \xi_K\) of the basis. For shape_unimodal() the slopes of the coefficients are \(\pm g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\), of one sign up to \(M\) and of the other after it, so the coefficients, and with them the curve, have a single extremum; \(M = 1\) and \(M = K\) are monotone curves. For shape_sigmoid() every slope has the sign of the shape: the slope at each end is constrained, and the second divided differences are summed from each end toward the inflection, up to index \(M\) from the left and down to \(M + 1\) from the right, so the slopes grow in absolute value up to the inflection and shrink after it; \(M\) runs from 2 to \(K\).

The penalty of scs() is one random walk on \(\gamma\) across the location, whose null space is the same for every \(M\), so fits at different \(M\) are compared by their criterion.

How the location is chosen

With mode or inflection given, \(M\) is the index of the Greville abscissa nearest to it, and the model is fitted from two starts (the least-squares lines of shape_start() and the slopes of a smoothing spline) whose better criterion is kept: away from the mode of the data the first start is nearly flat and can leave the fit on the flat curve. Left at NULL, the fitting layer chooses \(M\): a pilot fit with s() in place of the term gives the abscissa nearest to its extremum (unimodal) or to its steepest point (sigmoid), \(M_0\), and the model is fitted at the indices \(M_0 - 2, \dots, M_0 + 2\) that exist; the best criterion decides (see term_pilot() and term_variants()).

Under a factor by

With a factor by in scs(), mode, inflection, index, valley and decreasing may be given by level, as a vector named by the levels (valley = c(a = FALSE, b = TRUE) gives a maximum in level a and a minimum in level b), and the point and the value of value may be given by level in the list form. A location that is not given is chosen by level (mode_by or inflection_by at "level", the default): the fitting layer moves the index of one level at a time, from the pilot indices of the levels. With "shared" one index holds for every level, and the versions are taken around the median of the levels' pilot indices.

See also

scs(), shape_increasing().

Examples

shape_unimodal()
#> <shape: unimodal, link = log>
shape_unimodal(mode = 0.4)
#> <shape: unimodal, link = log, located at 0.4>
shape_unimodal(valley = TRUE)
#> <shape: unimodal (valley), link = log>
shape_sigmoid(inflection = 0.5)
#> <shape: sigmoid, link = log, located at 0.5>
shape_sigmoid(decreasing = TRUE)
#> <shape: sigmoid (decreasing), link = log>

# Under a factor by with levels a and b: a peak in a, a valley in b, and
# one location for both.
shape_unimodal(valley = c(a = FALSE, b = TRUE), mode_by = "shared")
#> <shape: unimodal (peak or valley by level), link = log, one location for every level>
